name: Melancholic Fairy Queen

facts.text: Level 65, 30,000 health, a flying queen at Lough Gur. She appears only at night, announced by 'You hear the sound of trumpets in the distance.'
She calls five melancholic fairy guards and casts a 400 heat spell.
Bot chat: she sits by Lough Gur and looks like someone locked out of her own door.

story:
Lough Gur is ringed with old doors into the hills, and the Melancholic Fairy Queen sits beside one that will not open for her. She comes only after dark, to a fanfare of trumpets from no instrument anyone can find, with her guard of five behind her, and she weeps by the water until morning. The Ardee folk say she was shut out of her own kingdom on the night the courts quarrelled in the Cursed Forest, and has been waiting ever since for someone to let her in. She does not take it kindly when strangers come instead. Her grief is hot, and her guards are loyal.

When the Veil came down there were Good Folk on the wrong side of it, and some of them were royal. The Ardee folk say the Melancholic Fairy Queen was shut out on the night the courts quarrelled in the Cursed Forest: she went to the bargaining and came home to find her door into the hill at Lough Gur closed, and it has not opened since. She comes only after dark, with her guard of five behind her and a sound of trumpets from no instrument anyone can find, and she sits by the door and weeps until morning.

Her grief is hot. Strangers who come instead of whoever she is waiting for feel it as fire, and her guards, melancholic as their mistress, are loyal to the end. She flies; she has never quite touched this side's ground. Maldahar, the Glimmer Prince of Sheeroe, is said to ride to the edge of the lake on some nights and look at her from across the water. Whether he is a cousin from the other side of the Veil, a suitor, or a spy, nobody can say.
legend: Wait for the trumpets: she only comes at night. Her five fairy guards come with her; kill or hold them first, then her. She flies, so ranged and casters carry it. Her spell is heat: resists up. Be kind, the old hibs say. Then kill her anyway. Wait for the trumpets: she only comes at night. Kill or hold the five guards first, then her; ranged and casters carry it because she flies. Heat resists. Superstition: knock on the door in the hill before you leave. Nicknames: 'the sad queen', 'trumpets'. The Ardee folk say if the door ever opens, the trumpets will play a different tune.

loremasterTopic.text: She weeps by a door into the hills at Lough Gur that will not open for her. Trumpets sound when she comes, at night.

bookPage: From Derbáil of Ardee's list: Lough Gur after dark, if you hear trumpets. Grandmother said the sad queen went to the bargaining in the court wood the night it broke, and came home to find her door into the hill shut. It has never opened since. She sits beside it every night and weeps, and her guards stand behind her, weeping too. Grandmother always knocked on the hill when she passed, three times, softly. I asked why. She said: in case it is only stuck. I knock too. I have never told anyone that before.
